analysis:
I found no concrete security regression in these units. They are CI and release-pipeline changes plus documentation, and none touch provider runtime, encryption, attestation or coordinator wire code. This is not a full audit.

1. scripts/ci-tested-tree.py (lines 91-125, 128-153) adds tree-keyed skip records (`ci-tested-tree-<tree>-pcm`) for single-parent (squash) pushes and two-parent merges. A record is accepted only from a completed, successful run of the same workflow path in the same repository and head repository. Its event must be pull_request or push, and head_sha must be a valid SHA. A match requires the exact git root tree and a component superset, so a record can cover only identical content. Any API error still runs the tests. The trust model is unchanged: a same-repository PR runs its own workflow and could in principle forge a record, as the pre-existing docstring notes. The new reach is that a record from any branch's PR or push run can now skip a master push with an identical tree. I judged this CI-integrity, not a threat-model asset issue, and did not flag it.

2. scripts/ci-component-paths.py (lines 131-135) no longer selects every component for PRs into master. PRs are now path-selected, and full runs happen on master push. The tested-tree superset rule still forces a full run on push unless a covering p1c1m1 record exists, so coverage is preserved. The release gating in provider-release.md depends on that master-push run.

3. scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py (lines 112-120) allows workflow_dispatch on refs/heads/dev for dev-environment releases only. It requires RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=dev and a GitHub-verified source commit on dev ancestry, and the dispatched source must equal the dev head returned by verify_source. This assumes verify_source(api, source, "dev") returns the dev branch head SHA; its implementation was not supplied. If it returns something else, dispatches fail closed. The schedule-to-dispatch handoff in release-dev-branch.yml and release-provider.yml was also not supplied. The doc at provider-release.md line 499 onward says the scheduled gate runs without secrets, and that must be confirmed. The error message still says 'push', which is cosmetic.

4. docs/operations/provider-release.md (lines 902-1204) is documentation only: cluster-runtime variable gating, catalog limits, signing-certificate rotation and rollback. It adds no new control. Rollout ordering depends on external coordinator work (darkbloom-platform#643) that cannot be verified here.

Remaining questions for integration: the workflow files that consume `tree-name` and upload records, the verify_source return value, and environment protections on the dev dispatch.
